source: NEC press release: Meta, NEC, and Sumitomo Electric to Collaborate on "Petal," (09-22-2026)

players.product: D-Wave annealing quantum computing customer and global reseller of D-Wave's Leap service (Japan, Australia)

quarterly_data.signal: Meta, NEC and Sumitomo Electric started collaboration to build 'Petal', which the companies call the world's first commercial petabit optical submarine cable system: a transatlantic system of approximately 7,000 km between the United States and France, scheduled to commence operation in 2029, using two-core fiber with 48 pairs of spatial channels (core-pairs) and a reduced-power single-housing repeater, to double the capacity of Anjana (the companies' transoceanic 24 fiber-pair system). Meta will fund and operate the cable system; NEC is responsible for the overall design and construction of the two-core system; Sumitomo Electric provides the two-core fiber. Eduardo Mateo (Chief Strategy Officer, Submarine Network Division): petabit-per-second capacity across a transoceanic system is a major technological milestone.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 7,000 km; operation scheduled 2029; 48 core-pairs; double the capacity of Anjana (24 fiber pairs)
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: customer (funds and operates the cable system)
